chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Arranger Nesbitt's drinking and mental collapse
summary: Nesbitt, the McKinney's Cotton Pickers trumpeter-arranger who wrote 'Chinatown' for Fletcher, drank and his arrangement fell apart in rehearsal into wrong keys without his noticing.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: That's a good question you asked, because there was a guy that used to write terrific. You remember an old tune, "Chinatown?"

"Chinatown, my China, China-town, one of those things. There was a guy named Nesbitt that did a gang of arranging for McKinney's Cottonpickers. This was even before Don Redman (unintelligible). Nesbitt, he was a trumpet player. Man, he was -- he got real popular, as he was an arranger and everything. And he was the one that brought that old tune back, man, Chinatown, you know. He made arrangements for Fletcher like mad. And then the thing happened. He got so that he was an excessive drinker, unfortunately. This is what

ruined his career.
But I'm going to tell you something that happened once. He brought an arrangement to Fletcher one time. I've forgotten the name of the tune, or the arrangement, whatever it was. But I know what went on. The band got to playing, and to man, and they played the first chorus, just started swinging and everything, and all of a sudden his mind must have snapped somewhere along the way. It went off into another key, mistakes and all this, and it wasn't the same tune and all that. You know? And the guy began to disintegrate like that in his mind, you know, and it got so that he went crazy.
Wow. And it actually showed up in his arranging.
It showed up in his work,

Man, he went off; the arrangements just quit swinging. They went off into something didn't make sense, and the guys quit playing. All of a sudden, they started looking at each other, you know, and there he was -- he was in front of the band. And, do you know, he didn't even realize that?
He wasn't aware of it, huh?
He wasn't aware of it. Well, he -- he was on his way then. So that was the end of him. But he was a great arranger at one time. Oh -- but this is what happened to Nesbitt.
